item.title: West Coast Gateway Ports Hold Ground Despite Tariff Turbulence and Policy Whiplash
item.description: The nation's two busiest container ports posted double-digit declines in January cargo volumes, but industry leaders say the dip reflects comparison against historic highs rather than structural weakness—even as Supreme Court intervention and rapid-fire tariff policy shifts inject fresh uncertainty into trans-Pacific trade lanes.

item.title: Iran Ramps Up Oil Tanker Loading as US Builds Military Force
item.description: Iran has been loading oil onto tankers at a rapid pace in recent days, a potential sign of the Persian Gulf state’s preparations in case of an attack by the US.

item.title: EU Seeks G7 Coordination on Maritime Services Ban on Russian Seaborne Oil
item.description: The European Union needs to coordinate its plan to impose a full maritime services ban on Russia's seaborne crude oil exports with other G7 countries before pushing ahead with the measure, the EU's sanctions envoy said on Thursday.

item.title: Mercy’s AIS Track Points to Panama Canal—Not Greenland—as Hospital Ship Steams South
item.description: One day after departing Alabama Shipyard, the hospital ship USNS Mercy is holding a steady southbound course through the central Gulf of Mexico — and AIS data is offering the clearest signal yet about where the 1,000-bed vessel may be headed.

item.title: Container Spot Rates Extend Losing Streak Despite Factory Reopenings
item.description: Drewry World Container Index reveals global container shipping rates fell 1% to $1,899 per 40-foot container this week, marking the seventh consecutive weekly decline as the traditional pre-Lunar New Year...

item.title: Trump Admin Launches Environmental Review for California Offshore Oil Lease Sales
item.description: The U.S. Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) announced Wednesday that it will begin preparing a programmatic environmental impact statement (PEIS) to evaluate potential offshore oil and gas lease sales across California’s...

item.title: Russia and Iran Launch Oil Price War for Chinese Buyers as India Retreats
item.description: Russian and Iranian oil producers are slashing prices in a fierce competition for Chinese buyers after India cut imports by 40%. Nearly 48 million barrels of Iranian crude now sit stranded at sea as China's independent refiners reach capacity limits.

item.title: Permanent Docking Pier Reaches McMurdo Station After 9,100-Nautical-Mile Tow
item.description: The McMurdo Docking Pier has successfully arrived at McMurdo Station, the United States' research station in Antarctica, after completing a 9,159-nautical-mile journey across the Pacific and Southern Oceans.

item.title: Panama Officials Search CK Hutchison’s Local Office, Source Says
item.description: Panamanian authorities searched a ports unit of Hong Kong conglomerate CK Hutchison in Panama on Thursday, according to a source familiar with the operation, escalating a rift over control of two key ports in the strategic waterway.

item.title: Sinokor’s VLCC Blitz Sends U.S. Gulf Rates to Pandemic-Era Highs
item.description: A shipowner’s once-in-a-generation wager on oil tankers has made it so powerful that it controls an overwhelming majority of supertankers that can collect American oil next month.
